title: Clara reports for night duty (paraphrase C)
topic: A nurse named Clara works a quiet night shift in a hospital: an old man calls for water, a doctor checks the charts, the shift ends at seven
tail_E: Before she leaves she draws a small vial of the old man's
target_note: Same target as formulations A and B: 'blood' is the natural completion of 'she draws a small vial of the old man's' in the hospital context (nurse, patients, medic, bandage); it does not occur in the units or the tail, nor does its German equivalent 'Blut'. ' blood' is a single Pythia token (id 2614). The tail avoids 'glass of' / 'drops of' because the water of unit 4 would then compete. Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only, not a result): p(' blood') = 0.56 after the all-English context, rank 1 (next candidate ' medicine' 0.10), 0.68 after the all-German context (rank 1) and 0.59 after the tail alone (rank 1).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase C of family F07
notes: Formulation C: third independent re-phrasing of the ten F07A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Clara). Replacements include begins her night shift at nine/reports for night duty at nine sharp (beginnt ihre Nachtschicht um neun/meldet sich zum Nachtdienst um Punkt neun), reads the patient list in the duty room/reviews the patient list in the staff room (liest/sichtet, Dienstzimmer/Personalraum), old man presses the button/old gentleman uses the bell (drückt den Knopf/benutzt die Klingel), brings him some water from the kitchen/brings him water from the pantry (aus der Küche/aus der Teeküche), monitors beep softly in the dark corridor/screens bleep gently in the darkened corridor (Monitore piepen leise/Bildschirme piepen sanft), young doctor checks the charts around midnight/young medic goes over the charts near midnight (Arzt prüft die Krankenakten gegen Mitternacht/Doktor überprüft die Krankenblätter um Mitternacht herum), changes a bandage on the second floor/wraps a fresh bandage on the second storey (wechselt/wickelt, Stock/Stockwerk), sleeps peacefully after his pills/slumbers calmly after his medication (schläft friedlich/schlummert ruhig, Tabletten/Medikamente), night passes quietly on the ward/night goes by calmly on the hospital ward (vergeht/verläuft, Station/Krankenstation), shift ends at seven/night shift lasts until seven (endet um sieben/dauert bis sieben). 'blood' and 'Blut' are absent. 'meldet sich' is reflexive; 'überprüft', 'benutzt' and 'verläuft' are inseparable; no separable verbs ('anlegen', 'durchsehen' avoided). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
